Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:1.english: One who is prohibited by a vow from [deriving] benefit from his fellow before the Sabbatical Year - [This means] that his fellow prohibited him by a vow before the Sabbatical Year began.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:2.hebrew: אין יורד לתוך שדהו - לאכול מפירות שביעית, דאסור בדריסת הרגל:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:2.english: He may not go down into his field - to eat from the produce of the Sabbatical Year, for he is forbidden from treading [there].

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:3.hebrew: ואין אוכל מן הנוטות - מאותן פירות הנוטין חוץ לשדה, שיכול ליקח מהן ואינו צריך ליכנס בתוך השדה. ואע"ג דהן שביעית, לא יאכל מהן, כדאמרינן בגמרא: אדם אוסר דבר שברשותו אפילו לכשיצא מרשותו. והאי נמי, כיון דלפני שביעית הדירו חבירו, כי אתי נמי שביעי' אסור בהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:3.english: And he may not eat from those that lean out - From those fruits that lean outside the field, which he can take from and does not need to enter into the field. And even though they are [produce of] the Sabbatical year, he may not eat from them, as we say in the Gemara: A person can prohibit something that is in his possession even when it leaves his possession. And [in] this [case] too, since his fellow placed a vow upon him before the Sabbatical year, even when the Sabbatical year arrives he is forbidden [to benefit] from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:4.hebrew: ובשביעית - אבל אם הדירו בשביעית, לא יורד לתוך שדהו:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:4.english: And during the Sabbatical Year - However, if he placed him under a vow during the Sabbatical Year, he may not enter his field.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:5.hebrew: אבל אוכל הוא מן הנוטות - הואיל ולא הוי ברשותו השתא כי מדיר ליה. ובגמרא מפרש אמאי אינו יורד ואמאי אוכל, הא ארעא נמי דהפקר היא:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:5.english: However, he may eat from those that lean [out] - Since it is not in his possession now when he prohibits him [by vow]. And in the Gemara it explains why he may not enter and why he may eat, [for] is not the land also ownerless?

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:6.hebrew: נדר הימנו מאכל לפני שביעית - אבל לא נדר הימנו הנאה, לכי מטי שביעית יורד ואינו אוכל, דהא לא הדירו אלא מן מאכל. אבל אינו אוכל כדפרישית לעיל, דאדם אוסר דבר שברשותו אפי' לאחר שיצא מרשותו:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:6.english: [If] he vowed [not to benefit] from his food before the Sabbatical Year - but he did not vow [to abstain] from benefit from him, when the Sabbatical Year arrives, he may enter [his field] and may not eat, for he only forbade him from food. However, he may not eat, as I explained above, because a person can forbid something that is in his possession even after it leaves his possession.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:7.english: And during the Sabbatical Year - He forbade him by a vow during the Sabbatical Year.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:8.hebrew: יורד ואוכל - דעכשיו יצא מרשותו. ואית דנפרש: המודר הנאה מחבירו לפני שביעית, לא ירד לתוך שדהו לפני שביעית ולא יאכל מן הנוטות, כיון דהדירו; ובשביעית — כלומר, אם הגיעה שביעית — לא ירד לתוך שדהו כו'. ולישנא קמא עיקר:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:1:8.english: He may enter and eat - Because now [the produce] has left his [the owner's] domain. And some explain: [Regarding] "one for whom benefit from another is forbidden before the Sabbatical Year" — he may not enter his field before the Sabbatical Year, nor may he eat from [the growths] that lean [out of the field], since he barred him by a vow; and "during the Sabbatical Year" — that is to say, if the Sabbatical Year arrives — he may not enter his field, etc. And the first explanation is the primary one.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:2:1.english: Who both say: "This property of mine is [forbidden] to you" - That is to say, "All my property is [forbidden] to you, wherever it may be."

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:2:2.hebrew: ואין אוכל מן הנוטות - ואע"פ שהגיע שביעית ושל הפקר הן:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:2:2.english: And he may not eat from [the branches] that lean [out] - Even though the Sabbatical Year has arrived and they are ownerless.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:2:3.hebrew: ואם בשביעית נדר - דהשתא לאו ברשותו הוא ולא מצי מדיר לה מנייהו, אוכל מן הנוטות:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:2:3.english: And if he vowed during the Sabbatical Year - Since now it is not in his possession and he cannot prohibit [him] by a vow from [benefiting from] them, he may eat from [the produce] that leans [out of the field].

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:3:1.hebrew: ר' יוחנן ור"ל דאמרי - הגיע שביעית, אין יורד, אבל אוכל מן הנוטות:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:3:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish say - [When] the Sabbatical year arrives, he may not enter [his field], but he may eat from the overhanging [branches].

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:4:1.hebrew: אדם אוסר דבר שברשותו אפילו לכשיצא מרשותו - דכיון דבשעה שאסר הויין ברשותיה, אפילו לכי הגיע שביעית נפקן מרשותיה, אפילו הכי אסורין עליו:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:4:1.english: A person renders an item in his possession forbidden even when it leaves his possession - Since at the time he rendered [the produce] forbidden it was in his possession, even when the Sabbatical Year arrives [and] it leaves his possession, even so, it is forbidden to him.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:4:2.hebrew: ר' יוחנן ור"ל סבר אין אדם כו' - ומשום הכי, כי הגיע שביעית דנפקא מרשותיה, אוכל הוא מן הנוטות:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:4:2.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish hold: A person cannot, etc. - And therefore, when the Sabbatical Year arrives, when [the produce] leaves his possession, he may eat from the overhanging [branches].

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:5:1.english: And do you think - that they disagree for this reason?

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:5:2.hebrew: ומי איכא למ"ד אין אדם אוסר כו' - ור' יוחנן ור"ל הכי סבירא להו:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:5:2.english: And is there anyone who says [that] a person cannot render [an item] forbidden, etc. - And [do] Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish hold this?

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:5:3.english: If so - That it is for this reason that they disagree and say that he may eat [from it] in the Sabbatical year.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:5:4.hebrew: ליפלגי בנכסים אלו - אפי' היכא דאמר "נכסים אלו עליך", ולימרו ר' יוחנן ור"ל דאוכל בשביעית משום הטעם דאמר אין אדם אוס' דבר שברשותו לכשיצא מרשותו, כ"ש היכא דאמ' "נכסי", דמשמע כל זמן שהן ברשותו! אלא מדלא פליגי ב"נכסים אלו" אלא ב"נכסי", ש"מ דלית להו האי סברא. ועוד, היכי מצי אמר לעולם דאין אדם אוסר דבר שברשותו לכשיצא מרשותו? והתנן דאוסר:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:5:4.english: Let them disagree in "this property" - Even where he said, "This property [is forbidden] to you," let Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish say that he may eat [the produce] in the Sabbatical year because of the reason that one says a person cannot render an item in his possession forbidden [for] when it leaves his possession; all the more so where he said "my property," which implies [only] as long as it is in his possession! Rather, since they do not disagree regarding "this property," only regarding "my property," conclude from this that they do not hold this reasoning. And furthermore, how could he actually say that a person cannot render an item in his possession forbidden [for] when it leaves his possession? Why, we learned in the Mishnah that he does forbid [it]!

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:6:1.english: One who says to his son: "Konam that you benefit from me" - That is to say, that you may not benefit from me, from any of my property.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:6:2.hebrew: מת יירשנו - שלא אסר עליו אלא כל זמן שהנכסים שלו, לפיכך יירשנו אם מת:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:6:2.english: [If he] dies, he will inherit him - For he only forbade [it] to him as long as the property is his; therefore, he will inherit him if he dies.

Rashi on Nedarim 42a:6:3.hebrew: ואם נדר בחייו ובמותו - כיון דמפרש במותו, מת — לא יירשנו. אלמא דאדם אוסר דבר שברשותו לכשיצא מרשותו לאחר מותו:
Rashi on Nedarim 42a:6:3.english: And if he vowed "during his lifetime and upon his death" - Since he specified "upon his death," [if he] died, [the son] does not inherit him. Thus [we see] that a person can render an item in his possession forbidden for when it leaves his possession after his death.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:1:1.hebrew: המודר הנאה מחבירו לפני שביעית לא ירד לתוך שדהו - דדריסת הרגל אסורה; ואינו אוכל אפילו מן הנוטות חוץ לשדה, דאינו צריך לירד ולאוכלם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:1:1.english: One for whom benefit from another is forbidden, before the Sabbatical Year, may not enter his field - Because treading [in the field] is forbidden; and he may not eat even from [the produce] leaning outside the field, where he does not need to enter [the field] and eat them.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:1:2.hebrew: ובשביעית - פי': אם הדיר בשביעית, לא ירד לתוך שדהו ליקח מן הנוטו'; (אבל) אם יצטרך לירד ולאכול, אסור. ובגמ' פריך: אמאי אסור לירד בו לצורך אכילה? הא רחמנא אפקריה לשדה לכל דבר אכילה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:1:2.english: And during the Sabbatical Year - [This] means: if he forbade [him] by a vow during the Sabbatical Year, he may not enter into his field to take from the leaning [branches]; (however,) if he needs to enter and eat, it is forbidden. And in the Gemara it asks: Why is it forbidden to enter it for the purpose of eating, since the Merciful One rendered the field ownerless for any matter of eating?

Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:1:3.hebrew: נדר ממנו מאכל לפני שביעי' יורד לתוך שדהו - דאינו מודר אלא מדבר המביא לידי מאכל, ואינו אוכל מן הפירות:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:1:3.english: If one vowed [to abstain from] food from him before the Sabbatical Year, he may enter his field - For he is only forbidden by vow from something that leads to food, and he may not eat from the produce.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:1:4.hebrew: ובשביעית יורד ואוכל - דהפקר הוא. וקשה, דלעיל (נדרים דף לג -) מיבעיא ליה אם מפסק ומיזיל בארעא אי הוי הנאה המביאה לידי מאכל. וי"ל דבשביעית אף השדה הפקר לצורך אכילה, דהכי מסיק בגמ'. ולאידך נמי, דמשני "שמא ישהה בעמידה" — הכא לא שייך במודר מאכל, דאי שהה אין בכך כלום:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:1:4.english: And during the Sabbatical Year, he may enter and eat - because it is ownerless. And [this] is difficult, for earlier (Nedarim 33a) [the Gemara] raises a dilemma whether stepping and walking on the land is [considered] a benefit that leads to food. And one can answer that in the Sabbatical Year, even the field [itself] is ownerless for the sake of eating [the produce], for so the Gemara concludes. And according to the other [explanation] as well, which answers "lest he tarry while standing [there]" — here, in [the case of] one who is vowed from food, [that concern] does not apply, for if he tarries, there is nothing wrong with that.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:2:1.hebrew: רב ושמואל אמרי נכסי אלו עליך לפני שביעית אינו אוכל מן הנוטות - ואף על פי שהגיע שביעית, דכיון דאמר "אלו", אסורין עליו אפי' לאחר שנתנם או שהפקירם, ולכך אסור בשביעית. והשתא ס"ד דבלא אמר "נכסיי אלו" והגיע שביעית — אסור לאכול מן הנוטות, דאדם אוסר דבר שברשותו אף כשיצא מרשותו; ומתני' דקתני "ובשביעי' אוכל בנוטות", מיירי בהדירו בשביעית עצמה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:2:1.english: Rav and Shmuel say: "This property of mine [is forbidden] to you" before the Sabbatical Year, he may not eat from the overhanging [branches] - And even though the Sabbatical Year has arrived — for since he said "these," they are forbidden to him even after he gave them away or declared them ownerless, and therefore it is forbidden during the Sabbatical Year. And at this stage [the Gemara] assumes that [even] when he did not say "this property of mine" and the Sabbatical Year arrived, it is forbidden to eat from the overhanging [branches], because a person can forbid something in his possession even when it leaves his possession; and the Mishnah that teaches, "and in the Sabbatical Year he may eat of the overhanging [branches]," is referring to where he vowed against him during the Sabbatical Year itself.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:3:1.hebrew: רבי יוחנן ור"ש בן לקיש [אמרי] "נכסי עליך", אינו יורד לתוך שדהו כו', הגיע שביעית אוכל מן הנוטות - והפקר הן, ולא אסרן אלא כי איתנהו לדידיה, אבל אי יהבינהו [לא], דאין אדם אוסר בקונמות לכשיצא מרשותיה, וה"ה היכא דאמר "נכסי אלו" הגיע שביעית מותר בנוטות. ופריך: אם כן, דלא אסר רבי יוחנן כלל לכשיצא מרשותו, אמאי לא אשמועינן למילתא באלו? אלא אית להו אדם אוסר, ועוד תנן דאדם אוסר לכשיצא מרשותו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:3:1.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish [say]: "[Benefit from] my property [is forbidden] to you" — he may not enter his field, etc.; when the Sabbatical Year arrives, he may eat from the overhanging [produce] - And they are ownerless, and he only forbade them while they are in his possession, but if he gave them away [they are not forbidden], since a person cannot forbid [property] through konamot [vows] for when it leaves his possession; and the same applies where he said "these properties [of mine]" — when the Sabbatical Year arrives, he is permitted [to eat] from the overhanging [produce]. And [the Gemara] asks: If so, that Rabbi Yochanan does not forbid [property] at all for when it leaves his possession, why did he not teach us this matter with "these [properties]"? Rather, they hold [that] a person can forbid [property even after it leaves his possession], and furthermore we learned in a Mishnah that a person can forbid [property] for when it leaves his possession.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:6:1.hebrew: מת יירשנו - דכשיש כח ברשותו, אוסרה ותו לא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:6:1.english: [If he] dies, he will inherit him - For when he has authority in his possession, he renders it forbidden, and nothing more.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:6:2.hebrew: בחייו ובמותו לא יירשנו - אלמא אוסר אחריו לאחר מותו, שיצאו מרשותו. ומשני לה: לעולם לא תפשוט מידי דהיכא דאמר "נכסי אלו עליך" שיאסרו לאחר שיצאו מרשותו, דשאני הכא שפי' בהדיא שיאסרו לאחר מותו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42a:6:2.english: "During his lifetime and upon his death, he may not inherit him" - Thus, he renders [his property] forbidden after him, after his death, when it has left his possession. And [the Gemara] answers it: In fact, you cannot resolve anything [from this] regarding a case where one says, "These properties of mine [are forbidden] to you," that they should be forbidden after they leave his possession, because here it is different, since he explicitly specified that they should be forbidden after his death.
